rappel_detail.anchor: slung rock horn or a fixed ring on webbing
rappel_detail.station: The head of the central gully on the summit pyramid, below the short summit-block downclimb.
rappel_detail.notes: First rappel down the central gully. Inspect any existing slings before trusting them.
hazards: The gully is a rockfall corridor, especially with several parties in it.

rappel_detail.anchor: slung horn or a fixed station
rappel_detail.station: A lower station in the central gully.
rappel_detail.notes: Down to the base of the summit pyramid; some seasons need a third gully rappel. A 60 m rope reaches farther between stations and cuts down on exposed downclimbing. From the base, traverse to the top of Hell's Highway, which is usually downclimbed (a short rappel is an option).

rappel_detail.anchor: picket in snow or ice (bring your own)
rappel_detail.station: The top of Winnie's Slide, reached by reversing the Upper Curtis Glacier traverse.
rappel_detail.notes: Optional. Winnie's Slide is usually downclimbed facing in with pickets for protection; rappel it when it is too icy to downclimb.
hazards: Pickets left by earlier parties are often pulled by later ones, so do not count on finding one in place.

rappel_detail.station: The lower Fisher Chimneys, below the mostly downclimbable 3rd/4th-class upper chimneys.
rappel_detail.notes: The lowest steps of the chimneys have fixed rappel anchors and are commonly rappelled rather than downclimbed; this may take more than one rappel.

set.rappels: About 4 rappels on an average descent, by snow cover and how much the party downclimbs: the summit pyramid gully, Winnie's Slide if icy, and the lowest Fisher Chimneys steps
set.rappel_count_note: The full summit-to-Lake Ann descent takes anywhere from two to six rappels depending on snow cover, season, and the party's comfort downclimbing exposed 4th class; four is a typical trip, and the table lists those four places. Rappel lengths are not published.
set.descent_text: Reverse the ascent line in its entirety. From the true summit, downclimb the short 3rd/4th-class summit block to the head of the central gully, then descend via a mix of downclimbing and roughly two or three rappels off established stations — slung rock horns and existing fixed rings or webbing (inspect any tat before trusting it, and be ready to back it up) — to the base of the summit pyramid. A single 60m rope works and cuts down on exposed downclimbing. Traverse to Hell's Highway, a roughly 60m ramp of steep snow or alpine ice, and downclimb it (or make a short rappel) back onto the Upper Curtis Glacier, then reverse the glacier traverse to the top of Winnie's Slide. Winnie's Slide is a sustained, often icy snow/ice slope usually downclimbed facing-in with pickets for protection; parties uncomfortable downclimbing it will instead rig a picket rappel — but be aware pickets left by earlier parties are frequently pulled by whoever follows, so don't plan around finding gear in place. Re-enter the Fisher Chimneys at the bottom of Winnie's Slide: the upper chimneys are mostly downclimbable 3rd/4th class, but the lowest steps have fixed rappel anchors and are commonly rappelled rather than downclimbed. In total, expect somewhere between two and six rappels for the full summit-to-Lake Ann descent depending on snow coverage, season, and the party's comfort downclimbing exposed 4th class — four is a reasonable average trip. Below the chimneys, retrace the climber's path and Lake Ann Trail back to the car.
